Repo: /Users/tr/prog/silicon-photonics — "SiPhon", a silicon photonics toolkit (Python 3.13, numpy/scipy, src/siphon/, tests/, examples/). Run code freely with: cd /Users/tr/prog/silicon-photonics && uv run python ... . The full test suite (uv run pytest -q) currently passes 144 tests. Report ONLY defects that matter: wrong physics, wrong math, numerical fragility a user would plausibly hit, silently misleading APIs, or tests that would pass with broken physics. Do NOT report style, docstring nits, hypothetical micro-optimizations, or missing features. For every claim, compute a concrete counter-example or cite the standard formula you checked against. Quality over quantity — an empty findings list is a valid result.
You are refuter #1. A reviewer claims the following defect in SiPhon. Independently verify by reading the code and RUNNING it. Refute it if: the claim is factually wrong, the behavior is actually correct physics, the docstring already covers it as a documented limitation AND it would not mislead a competent user, or it is trivia not worth changing. Default to refuted=true if you cannot reproduce the problem concretely.

FINDING:
{
  "title": "expected_tuning_power_mw's heat-only justification is wrong: red-shift-only locking averages FSR/2, not FSR/4",
  "file": "/Users/tr/prog/silicon-photonics/src/siphon/wdm.py",
  "line": 142,
  "severity": "minor",
  "claim": "The docstring claims that for heat-only red shift, redefining the target to the nearest resonance order red of the as-built resonance 'gives the same uniform [0, FSR/2] distribution'; in fact the red-ward distance to the target (mod FSR) is uniform on [0, FSR) with mean FSR/2, so for the physically common case (silicon heaters can only red-shift) the returned FSR/4-based power underestimates expected tuning power by 2x.",
  "evidence": "With as-built offset u ~ U[0, FSR), bidirectional locking needs min(u, FSR-u) ~ U[0, FSR/2], mean FSR/4 (function's headline model — correct). Red-only locking needs (FSR - u) mod FSR ~ U[0, FSR), mean FSR/2. Monte-Carlo (1e6 samples): mean bidirectional shift = 0.2499 FSR, mean red-only shift = 0.4998 FSR. A per-ring uniform [0, FSR/2] red-only distribution is only achievable with bank-level channel reassignment (barrel shift), which changes the statistics to ~channel-spacing/2 per ring, not FSR/4 — neither matches the docstring's claim.",
  "suggested_fix": "Either add a unidirectional flag (mean FSR/2 for heat-only, FSR/4 for bidirectional/pre-biased heaters) or correct the docstring to state that FSR/4 assumes bidirectional tuning (e.g. heater pre-bias) and that pure red-shift locking without channel reassignment averages FSR/2."
}

uv run python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
FSR = 1.0
u = rng.uniform(0, FSR, 2_000_000)  # as-built resonance offset red of target
bidir = np.minimum(u, FSR - u)      # nearest-order lock, either direction
red_only = (FSR - u) % FSR          # red-shift-only to next target order
print("bidir mean/FSR   :", bidir.mean())
print("bidir max/FSR    :", bidir.max())
print("red-only mean/FSR:", red_only.mean())
print("red-only max/FSR :", red_only.max())
# distribution check: fraction of red-only shifts exceeding FSR/2
print("P(red-only > FSR/2):", (red_only > 0.5).mean())
EOF
input.description: Monte Carlo of bidirectional vs red-only lock shift statistics

input.reasoning: Confirmed by direct Monte Carlo (2e6 samples): bidirectional nearest-order locking gives shift ~ U[0, FSR/2], mean 0.2500 FSR (function's returned FSR/4 is correct for that case), but red-shift-only locking to the next order gives (FSR - u) mod FSR ~ U[0, FSR), mean 0.4999 FSR with half of all shifts exceeding FSR/2. The docstring's parenthetical at wdm.py:142-145 claims heat-only red shift "gives the same uniform [0, FSR/2] distribution", which is mathematically false under any interpretation (fixed target red-only: U[0,FSR), mean FSR/2; barrel-shift channel reassignment: ~channel_spacing/2). This matters in practice because the toolkit's own heater model (tuning_power_mw, line 121) is documented as red-shift-only, making heat-only the default regime; a user would underestimate expected per-ring tuning power by 2x (e.g. 16 mW returned vs 32 mW true for FSR=16 nm, 0.25 nm/mW). This is an affirmatively wrong statistical claim, not a documented limitation, so the finding stands.
